questions.prompt: What is a situationally induced impairment?

options.text: A permanent loss of vision due to aging.
A temporary restriction caused by the user's physical environment.
A software bug that prevents a screen reader from working.
A color palette that relies entirely on shades of blue.

questions.explanation: Situational impairments occur when environmental factors, like sunlight or movement, temporarily limit usability.
questions.hint: Consider the difference between a permanent physical condition and a temporary environmental one.

questions.prompt: How does direct sunlight impact a mobile screen?

options.text: It washes out the screen contrast by overpowering the emitted light.
It increases the contrast ratio by acting as a backlight.
It changes the font size to compensate for glare.
It causes the colors to become artificially over-saturated.

questions.explanation: Screen luminance cannot compete with direct sunlight, causing perceived contrast to drop dramatically.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a screen when viewed outside on a bright day.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand how ambient sunlight degrades screen visibility.

questions.prompt: Why is strong contrast critical for a user who is walking?

options.text: It stops the device from bouncing.
It conserves battery life while moving.
It provides a buffer against divided attention and visual instability.
It automatically increases the volume of screen readers.

questions.explanation: Walking divides attention and reduces reading precision, making bold, clear contrast useful for quick comprehension.
questions.hint: Consider how physical motion affects the ability to focus on small details.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify how physical movement affects reading precision.
